notes:
Synced changes now appear on your iPhone while you're looking at the note — no more restarting the app.

**Fixes & polish**

- **Notes update live on iPhone.** Changes synced from another device used to sit invisible on mobile: the data arrived correctly, but an open note kept showing what it looked like when you opened it — even navigating away and back didn't help, only force-quitting the app. Notes now refresh in place the moment sync applies a change, from every path (opening the app, a live realtime update, a background wake, or a manual sync), using the same careful in-place merge the desktop uses — so your cursor and scroll position stay put. (Fixes #659; PRD Addendum 27 §X brought to mobile.)
- **The Journal opens at the top.** On iPhone it was landing at the very bottom of the day's entry on launch. It now opens at the top, and stays there while the page settles — unless you scroll first, in which case your scroll wins. (Fixes #660.)

**Under the hood**

- The gap was at both ends: the iOS shell never told its webview that sync applied ops (the desktop emits `sync:applied` from its shell), and the mobile bundle aliases the Tauri event API to a no-op stub, so the desktop's listener registered nothing on mobile. Both are now wired, plus a UniFFI applied-notes callback for the realtime doorbell path (which was discarding the applied set). `SyncOutcomeDto` gains an additive `applied_notes`. Also closed a remote-control gap found on the way: `live_sync_refresh`'s kill switch was missing from the mobile bridge's flag list and was failing open. The Journal scroll was root-caused to TipTap autofocusing the empty document before `setContent`, which maps that selection to the end of the replacement and reveals it; fixed at the source with a bounded late-layout re-assert. (#661.)
